record.paper_title: Ten Open Problems in Connexive Logic
record.original_question: Provide a sound and complete semantics for NL, the axiomatically presented connexive logic introduced by Everett John Nelson.

evidence.quote: Open problem 1 Provide a sound and complete semantics for the axiomatically presented connexive logic NL of Everett John Nelson, cf. [12].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Everett J. Nelson's connexive logic NL is the propositional logic generated by an axiomatic calculus in the language with connectives for negation, conjunction, disjunction, and an intensional implication (together with, in some reconstructions, a primitive binary consistency operator), in which Aristotle's theses ¬(¬A → A) and ¬(A → ¬A) and Boethius' theses (A → B) → ¬(A → ¬B) and (A → ¬B) → ¬(A → B) are derivable, and which validates the standard structural and connective axioms originally proposed by Nelson.

Construct a formal semantics S (e.g., relational, algebraic, or many-valued) for the language of NL, together with a relation ⊨ of validity, such that for every formula φ in the language of NL:

(Soundness)   ⊢_NL φ  ⟹  ⊨_S φ,
(Completeness)  ⊨_S φ  ⟹  ⊢_NL φ.

That is, exhibit a class of structures with respect to which Nelson's axiomatic system NL is both sound and complete.
artifact.status_search_result: The Stanford Encyclopedia entry on connexive logic and recent literature still list providing a sound and complete semantics for Nelson's NL as an open problem. A 2025 preprint ("Considerations on Everett J. Nelson's connexive logic") provides a sound and complete algebraic-relational semantics for a modified system NeL (NL augmented with a weak conjunction-elimination rule), constituting partial progress, but does not settle the question for NL as standardly reconstructed.

status_evidence.title: Connexive Logic (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
status_evidence.snippet: Everett Nelson came up with an axiom system... The system is called NL in Mares and Paoli 2019.
status_evidence.claim: NL is the axiomatic connexive system of Nelson; providing a semantics for it is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Considerations on Everett J. Nelson's connexive logic
status_evidence.snippet: the system NL originally regained by Mares and Paoli, once presented as Nelson does in his first work, namely with the addition of a weak inference rule for conjunction elimination, is sound and complete with respect to a class of structures.
status_evidence.claim: A sound and complete semantics is given for a modified system NeL, partially addressing the open problem.
